entities.summary: Dubrovnik was a flotilla leader built for the Royal Yugoslav Navy by Yarrow Shipbuilders in Glasgow in 1930 and 1931. She was one of the largest destroyers of her time. Resembling contemporary British designs, Dubrovnik was a fast ship with a main armament of four Czechoslovak-built Škoda 140 mm (5.5 in) guns in single mounts. She was intended to be the first of three flotilla leaders built for Yugoslavia, but was the only one completed. During her service with the Royal Yugoslav Navy, Dubrovnik undertook several peacetime cruises through the Mediterranean, the Turkish Straits and the Black Sea.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Dubrovnik's construction and service with the Royal Yugoslav Navy marked a significant moment in Yugoslavia's naval development, reflecting the country's growing regional influence during the interwar period. Her completion was intended to be part of a larger flotilla leader program.
